es.summary: El síndrome de malabsorción es la incapacidad del intestino delgado para absorber nutrientes, provocando pérdida de peso, diarrea y deficiencias nutricionales.
key_points: Pérdida de nutrientes por daño o resección del intestino delgado
Diarrea crónica y esteatorrea son signos típicos
Causas comunes: enfermedad celíaca, intolerancia a la lactosa, intestino corto, enfermedad de Whipple
Se diagnostica con pruebas de laboratorio, estudios de heces y biopsia intestinal
El tratamiento se basa en corregir la causa y suplementar nutrientes deficientes

pathophysiology: Daño o alteración de la mucosa del intestino delgado reduce la superficie de absorción
Enzimas digestivas o transportadores de nutrientes quedan insuficientes
Los nutrientes no absorbidos permanecen en el lumen y causan diarrea osmótica
La pérdida continua lleva a déficit calórico y de vitaminas/minerales
risk_factors: Medicamentos que alteran la mucosa (p. ej. antibióticos de amplio espectro)
signs_symptoms: Pérdida de peso y masa corporal
Fatiga por anemia o deficiencia de vitaminas
diagnostics: Análisis de sangre: anemia, bajo albúmina, electrolitos alterados
Estudio de heces: grasa fecal >7 g/día, calprotectina
Pruebas de absorción de D‑xylose o lactasa
treatment: Dieta libre de gluten para enfermedad celíaca
Suplementos de vitaminas liposolubles (A, D, E, K)
Enzimas pancreáticas o lactasa según causa
Antibióticos específicos para enfermedad de Whipple
complications: Deficiencia de hierro, folato y vitamina B12 → anemia megaloblástica
Osteoporosis por déficit de vitamina D y calcio
nursing_care: Evaluar peso, ingesta y pérdida de líquidos cada 24 h
Monitorear signos vitales y turgor cutáneo
Controlar laboratorio de electrolitos, albúmina y hemograma
Educar sobre dieta y suplementos según diagnóstico
patient_teaching: Explicar la importancia de seguir la dieta prescrita (p. ej. sin gluten)
Enseñar cómo tomar suplementos vitamínicos y enzimas con alimentos
Identificar signos de deficiencia (fatiga, sangrado, fracturas)
Instruir sobre hidratación adecuada y registro de evacuaciones

outcomes: Volumen de líquidos: ingesta ≥2 L/día mantenida durante 48 h
Peso corporal: estabilizar peso (±0.5 kg en 3 días)

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada 8 h
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar déficit hídrico y ajustar reposición

interventions.action: Ofrecer soluciones de rehidratación oral con electrolitos
interventions.rationale: Reemplaza agua y sales perdidas por diarrea

interventions.action: Elevar la cabecera de la cama 30° para facilitar la respiración
interventions.rationale: Reduce el riesgo de aspiración y mejora la comodidad

interventions.action: Aplicar crema hidratante en piel seca y enseñar autocuidado
interventions.rationale: Previene daño cutáneo por deshidratación

interventions.action: Monitorear signos vitales y turgor cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detecta cambios tempranos de hipovolemia

related_to: pérdida de líquidos por diarrea crónica
outcomes: Electrolitos séricos: Na 136‑145 mEq/L, K 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L mantenidos

interventions.action: Obtener muestra de sangre para electrolitos cada 24 h
interventions.rationale: Identifica alteraciones tempranas y guía la terapia

interventions.action: Administrar suplementos de potasio según indicación médica
interventions.rationale: Previene hipokalemia asociada a pérdidas fecales

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre alimentos ricos en sodio y potasio
interventions.rationale: Facilita el autocontrol de los niveles electrolíticos

interventions.action: Registrar síntomas de desequilibrio (calambres, arritmias)
interventions.rationale: Permite intervención rápida ante complicaciones

interventions.action: Ajustar la velocidad de reposición de líquidos IV según resultados
interventions.rationale: Evita sobrecarga o déficit de electrolitos

en.summary: Malabsorption syndrome is the inability of the small intestine to absorb nutrients, leading to weight loss, diarrhea, and nutritional deficiencies.
key_points: Loss of nutrients due to damage or resection of the small intestine
Chronic diarrhea and steatorrhea are typical signs
Common causes: celiac disease, lactose intolerance, short bowel syndrome, Whipple disease
Diagnosis involves laboratory tests, stool studies, and intestinal biopsy
Treatment focuses on correcting the underlying cause and supplementing deficient nutrients

pathophysiology: Damage or alteration of the small intestinal mucosa reduces the absorptive surface
Digestive enzymes or nutrient transporters become insufficient
Unabsorbed nutrients remain in the lumen and cause osmotic diarrhea
Continuous loss leads to caloric and vitamin/mineral deficits
risk_factors: Medications that alter mucosa (e.g., broad‑spectrum antibiotics)
signs_symptoms: Weight loss and body mass loss
Fatigue from anemia or vitamin deficiencies
diagnostics: Blood tests: anemia, low albumin, altered electrolytes
Stool studies: fecal fat >7 g/day, calprotectin
treatment: Supplements of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K)
Pancreatic enzymes or lactase as needed
complications: Iron, folate, and B12 deficiency → megaloblastic anemia
Osteoporosis from vitamin D and calcium deficiency
nursing_care: Assess weight, intake, and fluid loss every 24 h
Monitor vital signs and skin turgor
Control laboratory values for electrolytes, albumin, and CBC
Educate on diet and supplements per diagnosis
patient_teaching: Explain the importance of following the prescribed diet (e.g., gluten‑free)
Teach how to take vitamin and enzyme supplements with food
Identify signs of deficiency (fatigue, bleeding, fractures)
Instruct on adequate hydration and stool charting

outcomes: Fluid volume: intake ≥2 L/day maintained for 48 h
Body weight: stabilize weight (±0.5 kg in 3 days)

interventions.action: Record fluid intake and output every 8 h
interventions.rationale: Detects fluid deficit and allows adjustment of replacement

interventions.action: Offer oral rehydration solutions with electrolytes
interventions.rationale: Replaces water and salts lost with diarrhea

interventions.action: Elevate the head of the bed 30° to facilitate breathing
interventions.rationale: Reduces aspiration risk and improves comfort

interventions.action: Apply moisturizing cream to dry skin and teach self‑care
interventions.rationale: Prevents skin damage from dehydration

interventions.action: Monitor vital signs and turgor every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detects early changes of hypovolemia

outcomes: Serum electrolytes: Na 136‑145 mEq/L, K 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L maintained

interventions.action: Obtain blood sample for electrolytes every 24 h
interventions.rationale: Identifies early alterations and guides therapy

interventions.action: Administer potassium supplements as ordered
interventions.rationale: Prevents hypokalemia associated with fecal losses

interventions.action: Educate patient on foods rich in sodium and potassium
interventions.rationale: Facilitates self‑monitoring of electrolyte levels

interventions.action: Record symptoms of imbalance (cramps, arrhythmias)
interventions.rationale: Allows rapid intervention for complications

interventions.action: Adjust IV fluid replacement rate based on results
interventions.rationale: Avoids overload or electrolyte deficit

summary.0.quote: If you have a malabsorption syndrome, your small intestine cannot absorb nutrients from foods.

key_points.1.quote: The most common clinical manifestations of malabsorption are diarrhea, steatorrhea (fatty stool), fatigue, abdominal bloating and cramping, increased flatulence, and unintentional weight loss.

key_points.2.quote: Causes of malabsorption syndromes include: Celiac disease Lactose intolerance Short bowel syndrome.

key_points.4.quote: Medical treatment is focused on finding and treating the underlying cause of malabsorption, avoiding any food triggers, and symptom management.

sections.pathophysiology.3.quote: Complications of gastric bypass include gastric ulcers from NSAID use or smoking, dumping syndrome, steatorrhea , stricture, reactive hypoglycemia, and vitamin and mineral deficiencies.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: Nursing assessment of stool characteristics includes carefully observing and documenting various aspects of the stool to gather valuable information about a patient’s GI health.

sections.patient_teaching.3.quote: Nurses provide patient education on healthy bowel habits, emphasizing the importance of adequate hydration, dietary fiber intake, regular exercise, optimal positioning to promote bowel elimination, and stress management techniques.
